The block is the product's entry point for coding agents in user repositories. Ratified 2026-08-24, 158 tokens under o200k_base. Ratified text:

## Provenance

Requirements live in a Provenance graph. Plan changes with the graph and update
it in the same change.

- Plan: `provenance prime --quiet`
- New obligation: `provenance rules create --scope default --id rule_<slug> --requirement-id <req> --statement "<testable clause>"`
- Annotate implementation with `rule`, tests with `verifies`. Annotations move
  with code.
- To change a Requirement, Rule, or past decision, create a Proposal. A human decides each
  Proposal.
- Pre-commit: `provenance check --quiet` and
  `provenance coverage scan --path . --scope default --validate-rules`.
  Commit graph updates with the code.

requirements.description: Four record kinds, source, requirement, resolution, and rule, joined by typed edges: a source references the requirements it motivates and needs a resolution; a resolution resolves the requirement and produces rules. 'provenance traceability <rule-id>' walks the chain back from any rule. A requirement without a source is surfaced as a gap, not rejected.

requirements.statement: Define an annotation format that mirrors Statesman's existing contract metadata vocabulary for declaring rule coverage in external test code
requirements.description: Adopt Allure's label/link primitive model but use Statesman's own vocabulary. The annotation fields replicate what contracts already carry: name, description, tags (from Contract trait), rule code, coverage level, confidence, notes (from RuleContract join). Per-language native APIs (Python decorators, Rust attributes, Java annotations, JS/TS functions) all serialize to the same output format. Comment-based annotations as the zero-dependency universal baseline. Explicitly NO epic/feature/story -- Statesman is not a project management tool. The requirement tree provides hierarchy; Provenance derives structural context from the rule's graph chain. The comment form is the zero-dependency baseline that works in any language; per-language native APIs (decorators, attributes) would be optional sugar serialising to the same output (absorbed from deleted rule PROV-ANNOT-003).

requirements.statement: An automated ideation run must be budgeted and cancellable before it starts, idempotent when a step is retried, inspectable after it ends, and unable to change a canonical record until a human promotes the proposal.
requirements.description: Compressed from the 27 run-machinery rules among the 38 imported PROV-IDEATE records (the other eleven: six were tests written as rules, five superseded by bound rules by shipped rules) written for the Statesman cloud ideation runner and never built. Their themes, kept so nothing is lost silently: a run targets one artifact and posts participant comments plus a synthesis to that artifact's thread; a stable run id ties the work item, participant executions, comments, synthesis, proposal cards, retries and promotions together; an explicit status lifecycle (queued, running, synthesizing, succeeded, partial, failed_retryable, failed_terminal, cancelled) never reports a run with a failed participant as succeeded; an input snapshot records target, sources, graph scope, profile and prompt versions, models and budgets; maximums for participants, rounds, model calls, tokens, wall-clock and generated bytes are enforced before execution and fail the run visibly; cancellation and deadlines stop new work, keep finished output and mark unfinished slots; participant writes are keyed deterministically so a retried slot updates one logical output instead of duplicating it; failures carry the failed step, retry state and diagnostics, and unsafe output is recorded as a sanitized marker rather than posted; participant comments carry stance, strongest finding, evidence references, risks, objections, suggested changes, uncertainty and open questions, and a challenge names the comment it challenges; synthesis preserves consensus, contested claims, minority objections, evidence gaps and open questions instead of collapsing them, stays short enough to read as a brief, and emits typed proposal cards recording their origin comments, claims, evidence level, dissent, confidence and target, with duplicates merged or marked; a promoted artifact links back to the run, synthesis, origin comments, proposal card and approval event; the thread shows outcomes before transcripts, keeps raw output as secondary, and shows the persona label apart from the executing identity; a run reads and writes only inside its target's scope and respects source access and redaction. What shipped instead is the proposal, assertion and disposition model in the ideation records; none of the run machinery above exists.

questions.answer: The installer owns the section under the exact Provenance heading and updates it in place. A renamed heading means the user took ownership. See res_injection_block_owned_by_heading

questions.question: Which command injects the instruction block: init or skills install?
questions.answer: provenance init. The block is instructions, not skills, and must land even where skills are never installed. See res_injection_block_owned_by_heading

questions.question: Which authoring paths can report ASD-STE100 syntax findings before graph generation without a second checker?
Which ASD-STE100 syntax rules can a deterministic checker enforce without a human decision about meaning?
What permission lets Provenance distribute the official vocabulary and rule data that its checker needs?
questions.answer: Provenance does not distribute the dictionary. Interactive setup imports a user-downloaded official PDF, agent setup downloads it, and projects reuse the local import. Canonical decision: res_ste_local_dictionary_acquisition.

questions.question: Must graph generation reject every deterministic ASD-STE100 syntax violation, or can a repository select warning mode?
Which first-viewport design should the generated wiki homepage adopt: Search Launchpad, Domain Atlas, or Traceability Ledger?
questions.answer: Search Launchpad wins. Graft Domain Atlas's capped authored-domain browse structure immediately below search and Traceability Ledger's single exact-count findings call to action below domains. Canonical decision: res_wiki_homepage_search_domain_traceability.

resolutions.title: Broker audit trail and attribution backfill
resolutions.position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-AUDIT-001 through BROKER-AUDIT-003
resolutions.rationale: Audit trail requires structured tracing with project_id in every handler span, identity attribution on all mutations (user/agent/service/api_key), and content-addressed deduplication for contract versions.
resolutions.context: Codebase scan identified 3 enforcement patterns in broker for audit trail

resolutions.title: Broker authentication pipeline enforcement backfill
resolutions.position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-AUTH-001 through BROKER-AUTH-006
resolutions.rationale: Authentication is the first layer of defense. These rules enforce Bearer-only extraction, token type discrimination, RS256 JWT validation, control plane delegation, hashed cache keys, and JWKS refresh rate limiting.
resolutions.context: Codebase scan identified 6 enforcement patterns in broker for authentication

resolutions.title: Broker authorization and permission model backfill
resolutions.position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-AUTHZ-001 through BROKER-AUTHZ-006
resolutions.rationale:
Authorization model gates every handler with type-safe permission extractors (RequirePermission

), hierarchical scopes (admin>write>read), mandatory auth extraction, proposal state machine enforcement, JWT permission merging, and 32 fine-grained permission slugs.
resolutions.context: Codebase scan identified 6 enforcement patterns in broker for authorization

resolutions.title: Broker information leakage prevention backfill
resolutions.position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-LEAK-001 through BROKER-LEAK-003
resolutions.rationale: Information leakage prevention uses 404-not-403 for cross-project access (anti-enumeration), token prefix-only logging, and generic RFC 7807 error titles to prevent information disclosure.
resolutions.context: Codebase scan identified 3 enforcement patterns in broker for leakage prevention

resolutions.title: Broker infrastructure security backfill
resolutions.position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-INFRA-001 through BROKER-INFRA-004
resolutions.rationale: Infrastructure security enforces request timeouts (30s), fail-closed on control plane unavailability, PostgreSQL-only database protocol, and parameterized SQL queries across all 21 repository files.
resolutions.context: Codebase scan identified 4 enforcement patterns in broker for infrastructure security

resolutions.title: Broker input validation and safety backfill
resolutions.position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-INPUT-001 through BROKER-INPUT-003
resolutions.rationale: Input validation prevents malformed data and resource exhaustion. Progressive transaction validation, pagination limit caps, and startup config validation protect the system boundary.
resolutions.context: Codebase scan identified 3 enforcement patterns in broker for input validation

resolutions.title: Broker multi-tenant isolation backfill
resolutions.position: Each pattern should be tracked as a Provenance rule: BROKER-TENANT-001 through BROKER-TENANT-005
resolutions.rationale: Tenant isolation is enforced at three layers (handler, service, SQL) with defense-in-depth. These rules cover project-scoped queries, project allowlist, explicit ownership verification, cross-org prevention, and body/auth consistency checks.
resolutions.context: Codebase scan identified 5 enforcement patterns in broker for tenant isolation

resolutions.title: Convex chosen as backend over custom WebSocket infrastructure
resolutions.position: Use Convex as the backend for Provenance
resolutions.rationale: Convex provides reactive queries, server-side functions, real-time sync, and document-based storage without building custom WebSocket infrastructure. First-party WorkOS integration simplifies auth. Trade-off: 1MB document size limit requires normalized schema with separate tables instead of embedded sub-documents.
resolutions.context: Provenance requires real-time collaborative editing where multiple users see changes instantly. Options considered: custom WebSocket server, Firebase/Supabase, Convex.

resolutions.title: Immutable dispositions are the sole state authority
resolutions.position: Model proposal, assertion, and disposition as three immutable record kinds and derive effective state from them; do not persist a mutable promotion-state authority
resolutions.rationale: The mutable promotion_state column lost on four counts from the blocking review: caller-selected rather than verified; proposal mutation and decision append are separate shard writes that can diverge; builds_on lineage pointed at state that could flip under descendants; six ingress paths enforced different contracts. A global batch-disposal queue lost on the evidence that batch disposal never happened.

resolutions.title: One Markdown reading governs checking and serving
resolutions.position: Use the published page map as target authority and parse links with the server's Markdown options
resolutions.rationale: The separate plain-parser check lost because it treated a footnote definition as a broken reference link while the extended serving parser rendered it as a footnote.

resolutions.title: Domain placement follows the refinement graph
resolutions.position: Attribute each requirement to its direct and inherited domains and each rule through its producing requirements
resolutions.rationale: Direct-domain-only attribution lost because an unclassified child and its rules disappeared from the authored domain of their classified ancestor.

resolutions.title: Evidence site states are report findings
resolutions.position: Record the enclosing symbol and content identity beside each evidence site's file and line coordinate. A later scan resolves that anchor before classifying the site, and the classifications stay derived report findings
resolutions.rationale: A line number moves with unrelated edits, so the coordinate alone cannot re-identify a site. Storing the classification would turn a derived finding into canonical graph state the next scan would have to repair

inputs.summary: Glossary entries for evidence site, evidence anchor, and evidence path at commit 6ec714d

resolutions.title: One shared gap computation for every surface
resolutions.position: Port the wiki assembler's gap taxonomy into a shared compute_gaps in the store, add the contradicts-pair, open-question, and unexplored-topic kinds, and delete the wiki's private gap logic
resolutions.rationale: Letting the wiki keep its own gap logic lost because wiki and prime were already drifting and already disagreed on orphan detection. Having the shaping skill assemble the frontier from five list commands lost because it is the hand-wiring the design forbids.

resolutions.title: Graph ids are valid by construction
resolutions.position: Keep the id character decision in one predicate called by private constructors and handwritten deserializers
resolutions.rationale: Duplicated constructor predicates lost because they could drift, and derived deserialization lost because it bypassed constructor validation for stored JSON.

resolutions.title: Graph references use full verified identity
resolutions.position: Resolve revision text at issuance, store a full lowercase commit, and rederive repository, graph, and reference identities on every read
resolutions.rationale: Persisting a branch, tag, or abbreviation lost because it can move or become ambiguous; trusting recorded identity fields lost because the graph can be presented from another repository or with changed content.

resolutions.title: A human canonical artifact ratifies acceptance
resolutions.position: A human-authored accepted disposition naming an existing canonical artifact stands without a prior assertion
resolutions.rationale: Requiring every acceptance to follow a swarm assertion lost because a tournament winner is ratified by the human action that creates the canonical artifact, and the extra assertion made that flow impossible.

resolutions.title: Typed implementation bindings retire in place
resolutions.position: Removing an implementedBy declaration marks the owned canonical binding retired. Declaring the relationship again clears retirement on the same binding id. Reconciliation stays inside the rules the same spec owns
resolutions.rationale: Deleting the binding would lose why the rule was once considered implemented. Leaving it active would preserve a claim the spec deliberately removed. An equal declaration owner used by another spec does not broaden the retirement boundary

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: implementedBy removal retires the owned binding in place

resolutions.title: Init does the whole onboarding, identically on every channel
resolutions.position: provenance init installs the bundled skills and injects the instruction block in one run. Behavior is identical whether the CLI came from a release archive, npm, or npx, because npx provenance is the same binary
resolutions.rationale: A channel-specific onboarding step would make npx and a release install behave differently for no gain. Both the skills installer and init are idempotent, so re-running init stays safe

inputs.summary: Ben: init should install the skills; npx adds nothing distinct

resolutions.title: The injected block is lean and CLI-only
resolutions.position: Inject the fixed 160-token block ratified 2026-08-24. No ownership markers. The block never names .provenance/state; agents reach the graph only through CLI commands. Changes to Requirements, Rules, and past decisions go through a Proposal that a human decides
resolutions.rationale: Marker header and footer blocks were rejected as noise. A state-path reference was rejected because agents that open the shards flood their context window. Prohibition wording was rejected because it reads as if the product cannot change; the Proposal path states the same boundary as process. The block replaces the retired managed marker-delimited skills section that legacy cleanup removes

inputs.summary: Design conversation: ratified block text and the rejected alternatives

resolutions.title: Init injects the block and owns it by heading
resolutions.position: provenance init injects the instruction block. The installer owns the section under the exact Provenance heading and updates it in place. A renamed heading transfers ownership to the user and the installer then leaves the section alone
resolutions.rationale: The block is useful in repositories that never install skills, so it belongs to init, not skills install. Heading match gives an update path without the rejected markers. Inject-once was rejected because stale instructions mislead agents

inputs.summary: Ben picked init, heading ownership, and the decides wording

resolutions.title: Invalid confidence is not repaired
resolutions.position: Reject invalid graph scores and warn on invalid source annotations while retaining the annotation default
resolutions.rationale: Silent clamping lost because a repaired endpoint looks authored; aborting the whole scan lost because one malformed source comment should not prevent scanning the repository.

resolutions.title: Later decisions use the modern lifecycle
resolutions.position: Keep the retired promotion-decisions shard at the exact shipped-v1 audit and write every later decision as a modern disposition
resolutions.rationale: Appending modern decisions to the retired shard lost after ac661a2 changed the compiled audit from 76 to 79 rows and bypassed modern actor and assertion authority.

resolutions.title: Mirror Statesman contract metadata vocabulary in external test annotations
resolutions.position: Use Allure's label/link primitive architecture but populate it with Statesman's existing vocabulary: name, description, tags from Contract trait; rule, coverage, confidence, notes from RuleContract. No epic/feature/story.
resolutions.rationale: Consistency: coverage data looks the same whether it comes from a Statesman contract or an annotated external test. The Provenance coverage model doesn't need to distinguish sources -- the fields are identical. No new concepts to learn for teams already using Statesman contracts. Non-technical viewers in Provenance see the same metadata (description, tags, coverage level) regardless of how coverage was established. Avoids positioning Statesman as a PM tool.
resolutions.context: External test annotations need a vocabulary for describing tests and linking them to rules. Three options considered: (1) invent new annotation-specific fields, (2) adopt Allure's epic/feature/story hierarchy, (3) replicate the fields that Statesman contracts already carry. Allure's label/link primitive model is sound, but Allure's organizational labels (epic/feature/story) are project management concepts that conflict with Statesman's strategic positioning.

resolutions.title: Only default generated output updates gitignore
resolutions.position: Append .provenance/wiki/ only when the caller omits --out
resolutions.rationale: Automatic gitignore mutation for caller-selected output paths lost because explicit paths are caller-owned rather than a repository-generated default.

resolutions.title: Pinned graphs project asserted scope only
resolutions.position: Project only canonical families of the selected scope, stripping collaboration fields on export and refusing excluded or foreign-scope records on import
resolutions.rationale: Exporting the repository wholesale lost because discussion and unfinished ideation are not graph assertions; foreign-scope records lost because one scope's digest and counts would describe mixed ownership.

resolutions.title: Posting reconciles active threads
resolutions.position: Select the oldest active thread by created_at and id, then archive every other active sibling in the posting write
resolutions.rationale: Refusing the post lost to the reconcile option in imported PROV-IDEATE-032; the shipped path accepts the post and repairs duplicate active siblings under the publication lock.

resolutions.title: Add proof as a sixth verification method
resolutions.position: Extend the verification methods with proof: a machine-checked proof outside the test runner backs the rule, and the marked site is the bridge that pins the implementation to the proved model.
resolutions.rationale: The cmdcache adoption experiment tried several formal-verification strategies and settled on Lean 4: a hand model with total injectivity proofs, an Aeneas extraction spike, and a golden-vector conformance test binding the Rust implementation to the model. Conformance understates that evidence; the word proof carries the claim. The proof checker runs in the adopter's CI; the scan reads the claim, consistent with how every other method word is trusted.

inputs.summary: The Lean 4 model proofs, Aeneas extraction spike, and golden-vector conformance bridge that motivated the sixth method word.

resolutions.title: Proposals are consulted on demand
resolutions.position: Consult undisposed proposals only through exact evidence-path or typed-territory demand and exclude them from Prime and global batch review
resolutions.rationale: A global review inbox lost because 153 backtrace proposals accumulated without batch disposal while the only reviewed section was disposed when work demanded it; inferred matching also lost because it widens territory beyond recorded evidence.

resolutions.title: Recovery trusts resolved cache children
resolutions.position: Resolve each transaction directory to a real direct cache child and operate only on that resolved path
resolutions.rationale: Trusting the marker pathname lost because dot-dot segments and symlinked leaves could steer whole-tree rename or deletion outside the transaction directory.

resolutions.title: Recursive requirements replace initiative/epic/story hierarchy
resolutions.position: Use a single Requirement type that recurses to arbitrary depth via parentId
resolutions.rationale: Requirements compose recursively via bind (refinement produces sub-requirements). The hierarchy IS the recursion -- no separate concepts needed. This follows the monad pattern: each requirement is a unit of work that can be decomposed further. Status flows naturally from leaves to root. Cross-domain sharing works via edges (depends_on, contradicts) between any nodes in the tree.
resolutions.context: Traditional project management uses distinct container types (initiative, epic, story, task). Provenance needed a way to decompose work at arbitrary depth without artificial tier limits.

resolutions.title: Resolution inputs are named, not graph-resolved
resolutions.position: Require nonblank reference and summary text without requiring the reference to resolve to a graph record
resolutions.rationale: Graph-only references lost because legislation, files, and conversations may stay external; repairing or dropping blanks lost because later text would falsely look like an original decision input.

resolutions.title: Review required is distinct from stale
resolutions.position: A restated requirement statement writes one review record per produced rule, naming the field, its value before and after, and when the change landed. A verification run arriving after the change clears that rule's review. Stale stays reserved for evidence whose code changed
resolutions.rationale: When only a sentence changes, no file moved and no test was touched. Reusing stale would teach readers to distrust the word. The record is the authority: plan reads it rather than inferring, and it reports previewed reviews apart by having no timestamp

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: requirement restatement raises per-rule review records distinct from stale

resolutions.title: The function is the rule
resolutions.position: A rule is a function in the codebase, or a type whose construction is the proof; #[rule(id)] binds it to its graph record, and no primitive, registry, or runtime exists
resolutions.rationale: Fiat's runtime and define_rule lost: a primitive earns existence only when something must call rules through Provenance, and nothing does. The OpenFisca insight (rules are registered executables) is kept without its engine. A wrapper on already-pure functions adds nothing; the attribute is the whole registration.

resolutions.title: A rule binds implementation, it is not the implementation
resolutions.position: A Rule is an independent behavioural obligation. The compiled rule marker binds the primary implementation to the Rule and does not define it. This supersedes res_rule_is_the_function
resolutions.rationale: A Rule must exist before code and survive rewrites, and Unimplemented must stay an ordinary derived absence. Both fail when the function is the Rule. The compiled-marker binding survives from the earlier position

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: rules are independent of implementation

resolutions.title: Rules follow human decisions, not code structure
resolutions.position: Rule granularity follows the decisions humans made: one function with many branches implementing one decision is one rule, and a decision with no function is a requirement whose rule is unwritten
resolutions.rationale: Rule-per-branch and rule-per-function both lost: the endpoint table is one decision with nine branches, and minting records for structure inflates the graph with entries no human decided. An active rule record with no function is a promise the scanner reports as broken forever - creating one to make a decision look landed is the anti-pattern the shaping skill must stop teaching.

resolutions.title: Keep Rust authoring semantics in provenance-core
resolutions.position: Place pure builders, document-decidable structural checks, address construction, canonical authored assembly, and the TypedSpec input family in the existing provenance-core crate.
resolutions.rationale: A new engine crate or SDK-owned materializer would duplicate ownership. Provenance-core already owns protocol and domain types, stays dependency-light, and is shared by store and wire consumers.

resolutions.title: Audit Rust crates before publication
resolutions.position: Do not publish the Rust crates until the DR10 audit covers public APIs, dependency closure, version coupling, engine identity, and MSRV, and Ben records a separate go decision.
resolutions.rationale: Publishing too early can freeze accidental APIs or an incomplete dependency chain. Graph promotion is not crate publication.

resolutions.title: Accept design-stage execution uncertainty
resolutions.position: Accept that Design review executed no code if V1 through V12 and the two Plan-entry checks discharge the uncertainty before reliance.
resolutions.rationale: The reviews establish ownership and controls from repository evidence. Tests and Plan-entry checks remain required before implementation claims success.

resolutions.title: Accept discovery-fallback risk with a fixture
resolutions.position: Accept the no-repository discovery risk with a fixture for the canonicalized start-directory fallback.
resolutions.rationale: CO-R7-7 closes the current test gap without changing discovery semantics.

resolutions.title: Accept the static empty-statement finding
resolutions.position: Accept the static empty-statement finding if V2 verifies the wire and STE rejection paths during execution.
resolutions.rationale: Independent code reading found no engine wire rejection, but execution is the final check.

resolutions.title: Accept error-wording risk with pre-capture
resolutions.position: Accept relocation-time error-wording risk only if current wire wording is captured before the kernel takes ownership.
resolutions.rationale: CO-R7-4 and CO-R7-5 separate engine-identical wire text from TypeScript-parity build-time text.

resolutions.title: Treat goldens as change detectors
resolutions.position: Accept golden files and corpus fixtures as change detectors rather than complete proofs.
resolutions.rationale: The fixtures protect named behavior while property, conformance, and existing engine tests cover other dimensions.

resolutions.title: Accept process-global host limits
resolutions.position: Accept process-global current-directory, environment, and advisory-lock limits and document them for in-process hosts.
resolutions.rationale: The first API keeps current engine behavior. Documentation makes the concurrency limit explicit.

resolutions.title: Accept publication risk behind the audit gate
resolutions.position: Accept publication-surface uncertainty only behind the DR10 audit and a later human go decision.
resolutions.rationale: Engine version, dependency closure, MSRV, and public API exposure can change the release decision but cannot bypass G1.

resolutions.title: Accept the heuristic purity check
resolutions.position: Accept V12 as a compile-time import check plus deterministic property tests, not a formal proof of purity.
resolutions.rationale: The checks catch the expected dependency and behavior violations without claiming a machine proof.

resolutions.title: Accept rejection-precedence risk with a fixture
resolutions.position: Accept rejection-precedence risk only if a multi-defect fixture pins the current per-item first error.
resolutions.rationale: Static call placement alone does not prove intra-list precedence. CO-R7-3 makes the stronger commitment observable.

resolutions.title: Accept stranded verification-run risk
resolutions.position: Accept that aborts, process death, or direct engine use can leave a verification run marked running.
resolutions.rationale: The facade records ordinary errors and unwinds before propagation. It cannot recover after process termination or bypass by direct consumers.

resolutions.title: Accept temporary TypeScript mirror risk
resolutions.position: Accept temporary TypeScript mirror drift while the kernel is authoritative and the cross-SDK corpus monitors parity.
resolutions.rationale: Deleting TypeScript mirrors is a separate change. V3 detects drift during the redundancy period.

resolutions.title: Use a thin provenance-sdk facade
resolutions.position: Add provenance-sdk as re-exports plus verification orchestration, macro projections, settings, a parity ledger, and engine_info().
resolutions.rationale: These are Rust frontend concerns that do not belong in the pure core. Keeping materialization, validation, identity, planning, and mutation outside the facade prevents a second semantic layer.

resolutions.title: Use Cargo compatibility for the Rust SDK
resolutions.position: Use Cargo semver for in-process compatibility and Cargo path or patch configuration for explicit development overrides.
resolutions.rationale: An in-process Rust consumer resolves crates through Cargo and does not need a duplicate runtime protocol handshake. Wire consumers keep the existing protocol check.

resolutions.title: Keep the stateful Rust seam in provenance-store
resolutions.position: Keep identity, reconciliation, ownership refusal, STE write gates, locking, planning, and mutation in provenance-store, and expose its SDK operations as in-process functions.
resolutions.rationale: The store already owns persistent state and one plan/apply path. A separate provenance-engine crate or CLI library seam would add another owner or lose store behavior.

resolutions.title: Resolve Rust implementation symbols in provenance-store
resolutions.position: Resolve implementation symbols to repository files in provenance-store and reject missing or ambiguous matches before apply writes state.
resolutions.rationale: The scanner supplies evidence, but the stateful apply boundary must own the decision and its no-write refusal behavior.

resolutions.title: Deliver synchronous Rust verification first
resolutions.position: Ship synchronous Rust verification first, record callback failure before propagation, and defer asynchronous verification.
resolutions.rationale: The synchronous API matches current engine operations and TypeScript failure semantics. Async support can follow without delaying the first native Rust surface.

resolutions.title: Preserve typed-spec wire semantics
resolutions.position: Route wire ingestion through the kernel at the existing pipeline points without changing protocol 4, schema 1, acceptance, first-error order, error wording, or decoded response order.
resolutions.rationale: Existing TypeScript documents and other wire consumers must keep the same engine contract while semantic code moves to its shared home.

resolutions.title: The SDK package supplies the engine
resolutions.position: Each language SDK resolves and runs an engine shipped as a package-manager artifact for the host, discovers the project from the nearest Provenance or Git root when unconfigured, and rejects engines outside its supported protocol range
resolutions.rationale: An install-script binary download adds a second distribution channel to secure and version. The package manager already delivers a per-host artifact with the SDK, so compatibility is decided by the protocol handshake, not by install-time trust

inputs.summary: POC outcome: façade plus one-shot child-process protocol; engine supplied by the package

resolutions.title: Simple key-value comment syntax, migrate to native annotations later if needed
resolutions.position: Use simple @statesman key: value syntax. If native annotations are needed later, a statesman migrate command handles the mechanical transformation.
resolutions.rationale: Comments should look like comments. The migration from one text format to another is trivial -- a sed one-liner or a CLI migrate command. Don't optimize the comment format for a future that may not come. The simple format is easier to type, easier to read, and easier to parse. Native annotations are a separate concern with their own syntax per language.
resolutions.context: The annotation format lives in comments. Two syntax options: (1) function-call style like @statesman.rule("CODE") which mirrors what native decorators would look like, or (2) simple key-value like @statesman rule: CODE which is honest about being metadata in a comment. Function-call style has the advantage of being forward-compatible with native annotations but adds visual noise (parens, quotes) to something that is not code.

resolutions.title: Foreign install targets require force
resolutions.position: Classify targets by installer ownership and require force only before replacing foreign content
resolutions.rationale: Treating every symlink as replaceable lost after a0d5c31 removed foreign symlinks; f48d264 retained force-free replacement only for the installer's own canonical symlink.

resolutions.title: A source pin locates without full identity
resolutions.position: Accept 7-64 mixed-case hexadecimal source pins while keeping graph-reference commits full and lowercase
resolutions.rationale: Applying graph-reference identity shape to source pins lost because source pins are reader locators commonly copied in short or uppercase form; applying the looser shape to graph references lost because abbreviations can become ambiguous.

resolutions.title: Sharded JSONL in git with a stable-id merge driver
resolutions.position: Keep canonical state as sharded JSONL in git with SQLite as a rebuildable cache, and supply a custom git merge driver that merges by stable record id
resolutions.rationale: SQLite-as-canonical lost because git cannot merge an opaque binary. Dolt lost because it needs its own storage layer and sync path and still cannot resolve same-field conflicts. One JSON file per record lost on volume at Statesman/SCHADS rule counts. Raw git line merge lost because one record is one line, the wrong merge granularity.

resolutions.title: Static analysis first, runtime reporters later
resolutions.position: Start with static analysis. Design the annotation format and Provenance API to support runtime evidence later, but ship the scanner first.
resolutions.rationale: Static analysis delivers the core value (traceability link from rule to test) with a single tool vs N framework integrations. It establishes the annotation convention that runtime reporters will reuse. The link itself is valuable even without pass/fail -- when a regulation changes, knowing which tests cover the affected rule is immediately actionable. Runtime reporters add richer signal but require per-framework maintenance (Jest, pytest, JUnit, Go) and higher adoption friction. Build the foundation first, enrich later.
resolutions.context: External test coverage linking needs a delivery strategy. Two approaches: (1) static analysis scanner that extracts annotations from source code without running tests, or (2) runtime test reporters (per-framework plugins) that capture pass/fail results. Both use the same annotation format.

resolutions.title: Keep automatic download for agent onboarding
resolutions.position: Interactive onboarding uses the official request form. Agent onboarding downloads automatically when no reusable import exists. Later commands use local data.
resolutions.rationale: Form-first remains appropriate for people. Form-first for agents lost because limited agents can stop at the form. One onboarding download is cached and reused.

resolutions.title: Acquire STE dictionary data without redistribution
resolutions.position: Interactive onboarding uses the official request form. Agent onboarding downloads the official PDF. Each project reuses its imported dictionary.
resolutions.rationale: This approach supports dictionary checks without publishing ASD data. It avoids repeated downloads and does not depend on a machine-readable release from STEMG.

resolutions.title: Use ASD-STE100 as the rule authority
resolutions.position: The checker applies ASD-STE100 directly. Provenance does not define a substitute language.
resolutions.rationale: A Provenance-owned ruleset lost because it would rename or reinterpret an existing standard and make its syntax findings nonstandard. Custom extensions do not affect the first implementation.

resolutions.title: Tests verify; only live code enforces
resolutions.position: Enforcement means the function stands on the live path so a violating state cannot occur; tests verify rules through a closed method vocabulary - exhaustion, property, examples, conformance, construction - and exhaustion over a finite domain is formal proof
resolutions.rationale: The binding-ladder model (tests as the weakest rung of enforcement) lost because it collapsed two relations into one word: a test stops nothing at runtime. Prover engines lost because checking every case of a finite domain is already a proof and adds a toolchain for nothing.

resolutions.title: Typed declarations retire in place
resolutions.position: A typed spec is a complete desired-state document only for records carrying its owner and address prefix. An omitted declaration is marked retired, keeps its stable id and history, and reactivates when declared again
resolutions.rationale: Omission is too weak a signal for deletion or ownership transfer, so both remain separate operations. Overloading a domain status would mix lifecycle with meaning

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: omitted typed declarations retire in place

resolutions.title: TypeScript constructs, Rust reconciles
resolutions.position: TypeScript owns pure declaration construction with immutable handles. The Rust engine assigns ids, validates and reconciles records, and materializes one canonical rule for a declaration shared across requirements
resolutions.rationale: Keeping construction pure means importing a declaration module changes nothing until an explicit apply. Letting the host language mutate canonical state would duplicate the engine's identity rules in every SDK

inputs.summary: POC identity rules: immutable handles, static implementation references, shared-rule materialization

resolutions.title: Disclose missing decisions and rules in the badge
resolutions.position: Render Resolved (no decisions or rules) without changing persisted requirement status
resolutions.rationale: Adding an archived status lost for this fix because it would change persisted state, and the first label Resolved (unbacked) lost because review rejected unexplained vocabulary.

resolutions.title: Plain text wins over speculative reference links
resolutions.position: Emit an anchor only for an existing web URL or a code path a recognized remote turns into a valid blob URL
resolutions.rationale: Repository-relative anchors without a known remote lost because they resolve against wiki routes and return 404; treating every bare dotted token as a path lost because prose tokens are indistinguishable.

resolutions.title: Unsupported layouts fail before conversion
resolutions.position: Compare raw stored versions with the supported constant before deserialization or shard mutation
resolutions.rationale: Letting Serde half-read a future layout lost because unknown fields silently disappear; leaving read-modify-write unguarded lost after review showed an unrelated create could launder a version-2 row into version 1.

resolutions.title: Unverified is absence, derived
resolutions.position: A rule with no verifies site anywhere is unverified; the state is derived by coverage scan and never stored
resolutions.rationale: Stored assurance lost: a persisted verified flag is the one copy that can drift, and the annotation-era self-asserted confidence field is the proof of what happens to self-reported metadata. Absence cannot go stale and cannot be forgotten.

resolutions.title: Verification bindings are canonical relationships
resolutions.position: Store a first-class verification binding whose stable identity is the verification owner, the canonical rule, and an explicit owner-local key. Method, repository path, and symbol are updateable facts on the same binding. A run is volatile evidence that cites the binding and snapshots its execution context
resolutions.rationale: File names, line numbers, and callback names change too easily to carry identity. No stored verified status: coverage derives unverified from the absence of both scanner-discovered sites and active canonical bindings. No Test node enters the generic ontology, because that would commit every language integration to a Test lifecycle the POC does not need

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: binding identity is owner, rule, and owner-local key; runs are volatile evidence

resolutions.title: Typed verification bindings retire in place
resolutions.position: A run is desired state only for the owner, file, and key it reports. Reporting a key in a file against a different rule retires the binding that key previously named. Absence from a run retires nothing
resolutions.rationale: One execution sees only the call sites it happened to run, so a filtered or sharded run must not mass-retire relationships it did not observe, and no run can retire another owner's work. Bindings whose recorded file no longer exists go to the stale gate instead, because a run that never executed the file cannot vouch for it

inputs.summary: Accepted ADR: a run retires only the owner, file, and key it reports; absence retires nothing

resolutions.title: Verification strength is a per-repo dial
resolutions.position: How hard a repository verifies is its own call: an examples mark on an existing test is a legitimate first rung that moves a rule out of the unverified list honestly, and proofs are the ceiling for decisions where being wrong destroys something
resolutions.rationale: A universal proof bar lost on adoption grounds: if every rule demands an exhaustion proof with an independent oracle, people write zero rules. The backfill of this repo is the ceiling demonstration, deliberately not the norm; the on-ramp is one rule in a PR that touches that code anyway.

resolutions.title: Warn on markers citing retired rules
resolutions.position: When --validate-rules is requested, coverage scan warns for every marker citing a deprecated or archived rule, and --strict treats that warning like every other scan warning.
resolutions.rationale: A retired rule no longer establishes current coverage, so silently accepting its markers creates false confidence. The warning names the rule id and its stored status, so a reader can tell it apart from a marker citing an id no rule carries.

resolutions.title: Stable-id chips distinguish colliding titles
resolutions.position: Render the shortest distinguishing stable-id suffix and add record kind only when equal ids occur across kinds
resolutions.rationale: A distinguishing prose clause lost when provenance-c9m.7 selected one short stable-id chip implemented once in the central list renderer; history records no further comparative rationale.

resolutions.title: Search-first wiki homepage with domain and traceability grafts
resolutions.position: Make query-first retrieval the homepage's primary action; place a capped authored-domain map immediately after it; finish with one exact traceability finding count linked to dedicated detail.
resolutions.rationale: Search Launchpad won because it gives known-item retrieval the clearest first action and compresses well on mobile. Domain Atlas lost ownership of the page because taxonomy quality varies, but its authored-domain cards were grafted as the main browse path. Traceability Ledger lost ownership because a full metric sheet would frame reader documentation as a maintenance dashboard, but its exact-count assurance signal and findings link were grafted below domains.
resolutions.context: Human ratified the hierarchy after reviewing desktop and mobile prototypes: search first, domains second, compact traceability call to action last.
resolutions.enforcement: Homepage renderer order, scale-contract tests, responsive browser checks, and exact health-detail routing.

inputs.summary: Winning artifact: query-first hierarchy and search affordance.
Rejected as page owner; grafted its capped authored-domain browse structure.
Rejected as page owner; grafted one exact finding count and detail call to action.

resolutions.title: Wiki publication refuses ambiguous filesystem state
resolutions.position: Publish through a complete sibling stage, reject unsafe routes and unowned outputs, and leave crash residue for operator action
resolutions.rationale: Live-tree mutation lost because failure could leave a partial generation; journal syntax as ownership proof lost because it could authorize deletion of caller content; route normalization lost because it silently changed empty segments.

resolutions.title: Workflowd runs the typed product loop
resolutions.position: Workflowd adopts the typed spec as the ordinary change path: the spec models obligations chosen from product intent, planning a changed obligation explains its impact, and the agent updates traceability in the same change
resolutions.rationale: A separate manual repair step after each change is the failure the loop exists to remove. One declaration per implementation detail would turn the spec into an inventory nobody reviews

inputs.summary: Typed product-loop direction and the workflowd dogfood epic, 2026-08-12

rules.description: The record kind is added when the ids match across kinds; an uncontested title shows nothing. Verified by property including chip minimality. Amended 2026-08-10: enforcement is now genuinely per page - one renderer sees every titled link a page renders, including decision titles, citations, and classification rows, so cross-section collisions get chips.
rules.statement: Two links sharing a title but meaning different records each show the shortest ending of their id that tells them apart, never fewer than eight characters

rules.name: Anchor resolves before site classification
rules.description: The classification is a derived report finding. No evidence-site state is written to canonical graph state.
rules.statement: A scan resolves an evidence site's anchor before it classifies the site as unchanged, new, moved, or gone

rules.description: Identical content passes; records behind no assertion change freely. Two readings of cited: a contribution through the claim ids an assertion supports, a synthesis packet by the id it names - both are uses of one shared core, so the freeze cannot drift between kinds. Import hand-derives the same freeze and drifted on deletion (tracked in beads).
rules.statement: A record cited by an assertion cannot be replaced with different content

rules.description: The sibling of rule_asserted_evidence_immutable: import stands a whole scope in place of the stored one, so it is the only path that can drop a record; a dropped cited contribution and a dropped asserted synthesis packet now error identically. Citedness is read with the store's own predicates, so the freeze and the deletion rule ask the same question.
rules.statement: A record cited by an assertion cannot be deleted

rules.description: Resolved and archived threads never win, and a record with no active thread has no canonical thread. Verified by property over generated thread lists with deliberate ties. The live path in thread_writers also archives the losing active siblings; that archiving is now rule_thread_siblings_archived, marked and property-verified. Supersedes imported rule PROV-IDEATE-032 jointly with rule_thread_siblings_archived: concurrent posting on one parent must leave exactly one active thread.
rules.statement: choose_canonical_active_thread picks the oldest active thread as canonical, breaking created_at ties by lower id

rules.description: The dual of rule_claim_eligibility: entry and exit guard the same set of statuses, proven by an exhaustion test asserting claim_survives equals no-blocking-status over all six ShapingStatus values. Written independently of the eligibility predicate so the duality proof is not vacuous.
rules.statement: A claim does not survive its record leaving the claimable state: closing a topic, answering a question, or blocking it on a human clears the claim

rules.description: One decision over both status enums; the refusal names the state with the word the record stores. Proven exhaustively over all six statuses. The dual is rule_claim_cleared_on_exit, extracted 2026-08-10 with an exhaustion proof that entry and exit agree exactly. Review note 2026-08-10: the eligibility check now runs before proposal surfacing, so a closed topic in a scope with a corrupt proposal shard reports the closure rather than the parse error - a deliberate error-order change.
rules.statement: Shaping work may be claimed only while its record is open for work: a closed topic, or an answered or human-blocked question, cannot be claimed

rules.description: Channel split, deliberate: the graph channel rejects the record; the annotation channel warns on the line and falls back to the default 1.0. The two agree on the verdict and differ only in the remedy - a conformance test holds the scanner to core's verdict on generated values. Silent clamping was removed at conversion.
rules.statement: A confidence is a real number between zero and one; out-of-range values are never silently repaired

rules.description: Actor ids are audit attestations under repository access, not cryptographic identity proof. The default manifest ships an empty allowlist, which blocks every disposition (tracked in beads). Proven over the powerset of a two-actor universe crossed with the disposing actor and disposition presence.
rules.statement: Only an actor listed in the repository manifest may dispose of a live proposal

rules.description: Four conditions judged on loaded scope state by a pure function; write_disposition is load, judge, write under the lifecycle lock. Rejected and deferred decisions need no assertion. Proven over 108 points with a real artifact index, plus one example per refusal arm. Convergence with core's validate_disposition_links is recommended and tracked in beads. Amended 2026-08-10: an accepted disposition needs a prior assertion UNLESS its actor is human and it names a canonical artifact - a ratified tournament decision stands in for the swarm's assertion. Proven over 324 cases including the identity axis. Supersedes imported rule PROV-IDEATE-003, which asked that persona comments, synthesis, and proposal cards never become canonical records unless a human accepts the proposal.
rules.statement: A disposition is written only when its proposal exists and is undisposed, any named artifact exists in the scope, and an accepting decision follows an assertion or a human's ratified canonical artifact

rules.description: The published page list is the authority, not the filesystem. Deliberately out of scope: bare anchors, absolute paths, any URL scheme, non-md destinations, trailing fragments, and images. Reference-style links are covered (pulldown-cmark resolves them to the same tag); image destinations are not seen. Parser-option asymmetry between check and serve is tracked in beads.
rules.statement: A markdown link naming a local document must resolve to a page the docs site publishes

rules.description: Records with no domain group as Unassigned rather than being dropped, so nothing vanishes from the wiki. Rule-to-requirement attribution is single-homed: one forward pass builds the inverse map both the domains page and the rule page read. Verified by property over generated requirement trees, including refines_into cycles.
rules.statement: A requirement belongs to its own domain and every domain of its parents, and a rule to every domain of the requirements behind it

rules.description: Twelve field sites (sources, requirements, resolutions, rules x origin thread/message; topics, questions x claimed by/at) are written once in visit_collaboration_fields; stripping and rejecting are two uses of the same walk, so the lists cannot drift. Proven per field site with coverage derived by running the real walk, plus a property that strip-then-validate always passes over all 4096 site subsets.
rules.statement: A graph shared outside the repository carries no collaboration fields: export clears them and import rejects them through one shared field walk

rules.description: One count predicate behind three flag families (resolution inputs, canonical artifact pair, source ref clause); refusal wording stays at each site. Proven exhaustively over count tuples against an oracle that derives the record count from the maximum rather than the first flag. The proposals handler's target pair now routes through the same predicate, and blank input content is refused by rule_resolution_input_content.
rules.statement: A flag family naming part of a record must name all of it: required flags appear once per record, optional flags are omitted entirely or appear once per record

rules.name: The gate classifies, it does not review
rules.statement: The diff gate classifies an evidence path as untouched, touched, moved, or gone, and performs no review and no re-extraction

rules.description: Differently-spelled git patterns are deliberately treated as different patterns; matching them would need pattern semantics and risk silently not ignoring the directory. Idempotence and byte-identical preservation of pre-existing lines are verified by property. Amended 2026-08-10: an unreadable .gitignore now propagates its error instead of being treated as empty and appended onto.
rules.statement: A generated output directory gets exactly one ignore line, added if missing, never duplicated, whatever whitespace or line-ending style the existing file uses

rules.description: The gap kinds: a requirement with no domain, no source refs, no resolving decision, or no produced rules; a rule missing either producer (owner ruling 2026-08-10: full tracing needs BOTH a producing requirement and a producing resolution; the gap names the missing end); a resolution resolving nothing; a source nothing references; a reference to a record that does not exist; an unresolved contradicts pair; an open question; an unexplored topic. Single seam consumed by the gaps command, prime, and the wiki assembler.
rules.statement: compute_gaps decides what counts as an unfinished spot in a graph; a complete chain from source to rule with settled topics and questions yields no gaps

rules.description: Enforced by construction: the predicate has one home in ids.rs and an invalid id is unrepresentable as a StableId or ScopeId (private fields, no bypassing impls, hand-written Deserialize routing through the constructor). All four shipped JSON-schema patterns agree with the runtime on a 50-value boundary corpus, verified by conformance against the emitted schemas. DispositionActor.id is deliberately outside the rule (actor identity, not a graph id).
rules.statement: Every id in the graph is non-empty and uses only lowercase letters, digits, underscore, or hyphen

rules.description: One classification (target state x identical/different x force) with three shells reading the filesystem in their own terms - file bytes, symlink target, directory tree. Proven over all 8 state x force calls against an independent oracle: nothing the install did not write is destroyed without force, and force changes nothing where the user has nothing at stake.
rules.statement: Installing a skill never replaces something already at the target path unless force is passed; an identical install is a no-op

rules.description: Nothing branches on the answer - it is the one line a reader takes as the account of the run, so it must never claim more or less than happened. Proven over the powerset of per-file outcome kinds, with order- and multiplicity-invariance checked rather than assumed.
rules.statement: A skills install run is reported updated when any file changed, installed when files were only added, and unchanged otherwise

rules.description: Anything the user touched is left alone: a single changed byte in the frontmatter or payload fails the hash and preserves the file. The version inside the header line is intentionally outside the hash, so a version bump alone does not orphan a file. The AGENTS.md marker block shares the proof core (hash_proves_ownership) but is a sibling decision without its own rule yet.
rules.statement: A legacy skill file is deleted only when its embedded hash proves it is byte-for-byte what provenance installed

rules.description: This gate is the admission half; the byte freeze is the SHA-256 fingerprint in core legacy_validation. Known bypass tracked in beads: the gate reads the proposal's current state, so a coordinated row-plus-flip write walks through - which is exactly how commit ac661a2 broke the frozen digests. The missing half is frozen-audit membership, and nothing refuses writes to the retired shard at write time. Amended 2026-08-10: admission now requires frozen-audit membership (the whole set must hash to the shipped disposition digest), closing the coordinated row-plus-state bypass; the left-proposed check remains as an honest superset.
rules.statement: The retired promotion_decisions shard admits a row only when its proposal has already left proposed; it may hold only the shipped audit, never a new decision

rules.name: Missing recorded file is stale, not retired
rules.statement: A binding whose recorded file no longer exists is surfaced by the stale gate and is not retired

rules.name: No stored verified status
rules.statement: No verified status is stored. A rule is unverified when it has neither a live scanned verification site nor an active verification binding

rules.description: Dot, dot-dot, empty segments, backslashes, and control characters are refused by name, so a hostile or buggy route cannot escape the staged output directory. classify_route is the single authority on acceptance and decomposition; the writer only maps its verdict to an error. Deliberate tightening at conversion: routes with empty segments were previously repaired silently and are now refused. Review note 2026-08-10: a drive-letter segment like C: is accepted as a plain name; harmless on the unix target the writer runs on, noted for any future Windows staging.
rules.statement: A generated page is written only to a route bounded by slashes whose every segment is a plain name

rules.description: Enforced by construction: GraphExport has no fields for proposals, assertions, dispositions, contributions, packets, or threads, and deny_unknown_fields refuses a returning document that names one. The rule marker sits on the struct because only the type governs both directions. The Value-typed escape hatches (expression/inputs/review_triggers) were deleted outright on 2026-08-10, closing the leak route.
rules.statement: Only the canonical graph families travel in a pinned graph; collaboration and ideation records never enter the projection

rules.description: A pinned graph names one scope; its digest and counts are read as facts about that scope alone, so a single stray record would smuggle another scope's data into a handover. The first offending record is named in the refusal. Proven per record family (11 families), with the family list tied to the GraphExport shape at compile time.
rules.statement: Every record in a pinned graph must carry the scope id the graph claims, on export and import alike

rules.description: Applied at both readings: the claim's own type and the evidence records behind it. Proven exhaustively over all six evidence types, with a second proof that the SpeculationMarker vocabulary names exactly the non-positive set in both directions. The evidence-side call is currently unreachable as a rejection path because the claim-side check fires first; it stays as the binding of the second reading. Supersedes imported rules PROV-IDEATE-014 and PROV-IDEATE-016, which asked that every participant claim be labelled by evidence type and that an unsupported or exploratory recommendation never be stated as product truth.
rules.statement: is_positive_evidence_type accepts every evidence type except unsupported and exploratory; speculation can never back an asserted claim

rules.description: Those are outcomes of human decisions, not authorable claims. Proven exhaustively over all 28 state x link cases. Reachability differs by caller: the batch landing path and file validation hit it fully; the aggregate path guards it behind an already-proposed check for shipped-v1 tolerance; the CLI create path hard-codes legal values. The dead contradiction in proposal_from_input is tracked in beads.
rules.statement: A modern proposal is written as proposed and nothing else, and may not carry its own duplicate-of or superseded-by verdict

rules.description: The promotion_state column on a proposal row is a claim, not a verdict. A row that has already left proposed is frozen at what it claims; otherwise a human disposition decides (accepted, rejected, deferred); otherwise a recorded assertion makes the proposal asserted. Every proposal read applies this, so no caller sees a raw claim once lifecycle records exist. Proven exhaustively over all 56 classification cases. Supersedes imported rule PROV-IDEATE-020, which asked for a promotion-state lifecycle of proposed, accepted, rejected, deferred, duplicate, and superseded, with only accepted proposals changing a canonical record.
rules.statement: effective_proposal_state returns the disposition's verdict when a human disposed the proposal, asserted when evidence exists, and the row's claim otherwise

rules.description: Whole-graph semantics: any cycle in the builds-on graph rejects the batch, and the error names the proposal where the walk closed, not the full path. Diamonds and shared ancestors are not cycles. Verified by property over generated DAGs with injected cycles against an independent reachability oracle.
rules.statement: A proposal may not, through the assertions it builds on, end up building on itself

rules.description: The undisposed precondition reads the projected state, not the row's stored claim. Reported reasons are never fabricated: every evidence path was both cited and touched, every territory reason equals the proposal's own target. The two live paths currently disagree on which triggers they can fire (tracked in beads).
rules.statement: An undisposed proposal surfaces to a worker exactly when the work touches a file it cited or lands on the artifact it targets

rules.name: No project management labels
rules.description: Imported from the Statesman era and rewritten 2026-08-10 for this product: the decision stands, only the product name changed. Prose, not a bound rule - nothing enforces it beyond the parser having no field to put such a label in, where an unknown field warns.
rules.statement: An annotation carries no epic, feature, or story label: the requirement tree holds the hierarchy, and a rule's place in it is read from its graph chain rather than restated in source.

rules.name: Simple key-value comment syntax
rules.description: Rewritten 2026-08-10: the marker is @provenance; @statesman survives as a legacy alias so annotations written before the rename keep working, warned once per block rather than once per line. Prose, not a bound rule; the deciding code is parse_annotations in crates/provenance-scanner/src/parser.rs.
rules.statement: An annotation is a @provenance key: value directive inside a comment - no function-call syntax, no parentheses, no quotes - and the legacy @statesman marker is still read, warned about once per comment block.

rules.name: Rule field is the only required annotation
rules.description: Rewritten 2026-08-10 against the shipped parser. The old wording claimed name is inferred from the function; it is not - the scanner records the enclosing function separately as function_name and leaves name empty unless the annotation says one. An unreadable or out-of-range confidence warns and keeps the default rather than being clamped, which is rule_confidence_range's annotation channel.
rules.statement: rule: is the only directive that creates an annotation; name, description, tags, coverage, confidence, intent, and verification are optional, with coverage defaulting to full and confidence to 1.0.

rules.name: Function-scoped by default with file-level override
rules.description: Rewritten 2026-08-10 against the shipped walker. The old wording promised file-scoped annotations covering every test in a file and function-level overrides of them; neither was built. scan_file looks ahead at most six lines for a declaration and records no function name when it finds none.
rules.statement: An annotation block binds to the first function declared in the six lines that follow it; there is no file-level annotation scope.

rules.name: Multi-rule via separate rule lines
rules.description: Rewritten 2026-08-10 for the marker name; the shared-then-override reading is what parse_annotations does - a field lands on the last rule named, or on the block's shared defaults while no rule has been named yet.
rules.statement: One comment block may name several rules with one rule: line each; a field written before the first rule line applies to every rule in the block, and a field written after a rule line applies only to that rule.

rules.name: Directives bind only on comment lines
rules.description: Reactivated and rewritten 2026-08-10, then amended the same day when the binding lexer landed. Directives no longer bind anywhere on the line; the lexer gates on comment lines, so a marker after code on the same line is skipped. This is deliberate: trailing positions were where markers embedded in code and string lines produced false hits. The rule was originally deprecated in favour of the tree-sitter reversal (PROV-SCAN-010) that was never built and has now been deleted.
rules.statement: The scanner reads a file only when its extension names one of the six supported languages (extensions rs, py, js, jsx, ts, tsx, java, go) and reads a directive only from a comment line: after leading whitespace the line must start with //, /*, or * (or # in Python), or continue an open block comment. A marker trailing code on the same line does not bind.

rules.name: Line-oriented parser only
rules.description: Reactivated 2026-08-10 as the honest owner of this decision. PROV-SCAN-010 deprecated it in favour of tree-sitter with statically linked grammars; that was never built, the shipped scanner walks lines, and both the tree-sitter rule and its resolution have been deleted. Prose, not a bound rule; the deciding code is scan_file in crates/provenance-scanner/src/walker.rs.
rules.statement: The scanner is a line-oriented text parser with comment-prefix awareness: it does not parse ASTs, resolve imports, execute tests, or modify source code.

rules.description: The function validate_edge_endpoint is the rule. Its branches: a references edge is accepted only from a source to a requirement; a refines_into, depends_on, contradicts, or supersedes edge only between requirements; a needs edge only from a requirement to a resolution; resolves and spawns edges only from a resolution to a requirement; a produces edge only from a requirement or resolution to a rule. Any triple not matched by a branch is rejected, so no edge may leave a rule and only a produces edge may end at one.
rules.statement: Every edge triple is checked against the endpoint table and rejected with InvalidEdgeEndpoint when its endpoints do not match its type's row

rules.name: Scan-time stale annotation validation
rules.description: Amended 2026-08-12 by res_warn_on_retired_rule_markers to add the retired-rule warning. The unknown-id and retired-status warnings stay distinct: one says the record is absent, the other says it exists and has been withdrawn.
rules.statement: The scanner checks every annotation and every #[rule] or #[verifies] attribute against the rules in the scope when validation is requested (--validate-rules), and warns twice over: on an id no rule carries, so a marker cannot manufacture coverage for a rule that does not exist, and on a marker citing a deprecated or archived rule, naming its status, because a retired rule no longer establishes current coverage.

rules.name: JSON scanner output format
rules.description: Rewritten 2026-08-10 against CoverageReport in crates/provenance-core/src/coverage.rs. The old wording named project_id, scanned_at, and tests_found, none of which exist: the report is pinned by commit, counts annotations rather than tests, and carries the attribute bindings the cloud format had no place for.
rules.statement: A coverage scan produces one JSON report: commit, files_scanned, total_annotations, a warnings array, an annotations array (rule id, file, line, function, coverage, confidence), and a bindings array (rule id, file, line, item, verification method).

rules.description: Crash residue is reported for operator choice, never silently adopted or deleted - proven over all 128 output-kind x artifact-residue states with the output and residue asserted byte-for-byte untouched after every refusal (unix; Windows keeps the reparse-point example). The five artifact names are minted once in ArtifactLeaves. Amended 2026-08-10: a refusal now names every residue artifact present in role order, and an unsafe lock is a fact about a listed path rather than an early refusal hiding the rest.
rules.statement: Publishing refuses to start when the output is not a real directory or when leftover artifacts from an interrupted run are present

rules.description: The decision is seven facts evaluated in one function: the must path (a qualified proposal cannot be left unasserted) reads all seven from records; the may path (an assertion is allowed) passes three as witnessed by the assertion record itself. Proven over all 128 fact assignments, with every refusal blaming a genuinely unmet fact. Replaced a drifted inline copy in swarm-backtrace preflight that rejected runs the store would accept.
rules.statement: A synthesis packet qualifies a proposal for assertion only when it owns the proposal's target, adjudicates that proposal and no other, and the proposal's cited claims stand uncontested with no blocking gap and no pending human decision

rules.description: The choke point where a stored line becomes a record guards every family - a hand-edited version-2 row fails list, check, and export instead of loading silently. A line with no schema_version makes no claim and is left to its own deserializer; cross-scope edges are filtered before the guard so another scope's future data stays ignored rather than fatal. Known residual: StateStore::manifest() is still unguarded (tracked in beads). Amended 2026-08-10: the write path bypassed this guard - jsonl::mutate_jsonl_locked read shards with plain serde and no version check, so a create beside a hand-edited version-2 row re-serialised it from the fields the current struct recognised and dropped the rest, laundering into the supported layout the record every reader refuses. That read now calls the same guard on the same raw JSON before any mutation, so a refusal leaves the shard byte-identical; the exhaustion proof runs all three loaders. Remaining unguarded readers of stored content, all non-lossy Value round-trips: merge's reader, the import scope-writer's edge re-read, and StateStore::manifest().
rules.statement: A stored record claiming an unsupported schema version is refused before it becomes a record, on the read path and on the read every write is built on, naming the file, line, record, and both versions

rules.description: Absence counts as a value a side can hold: identical changes are kept once, a delete against an untouched record wins silently, and a delete against an edit keeps the surviving side and reports delete_modify. Add/add with different content reports its own add_add kind, and conflicts carry the base pre-image. Proven exhaustively over all 14 reachable (base, ours, theirs) cases. Amended 2026-08-10: the driver is wired via .gitattributes, a conflicted merge exits non-zero so git falls back to conflict, and merged edge shards are validated against the endpoint table before writing - the merge no longer launders records past the write gate.
rules.statement: merge_records keeps the moved side when only one side of a merge moved a record, and keeps ours and reports the clash when both moved differently

rules.description: One comparison - resolved candidate equals container/name - rejects dot-dot traversal and symlinks at once, and callers may only act on the returned resolved path. An already-gone mode skips the leaf probe when nothing remains on disk. Tightened at conversion: a leaf symlink at a sibling inside the transactions directory was previously accepted. create_real_directory is the ancestor half (the cache itself is real), cross-referenced, not folded. Amended 2026-08-10: the touched leaf must also be a real directory - a regular file named by a marker is refused up front rather than failing inside removal.
rules.statement: Recovery touches a directory only when it resolves to a real direct child of the repository cache's transactions directory

rules.description: Gates all three read verbs; a refused reference fails every verb identically and names the mismatched field. Every mismatch arm has a direct test; exhaustion is deliberately not claimed because the input is unbounded git state. Known gap tracked in beads: exact-export documents are not self-verifying.
rules.statement: A graph reference is honoured only if its commit exists here, the repository identity matches, the graph at that commit hashes to the recorded digest, and the id is the hash of exactly those parts

rules.description: Version 1; grf1_/git1_ identities of exactly 64 lowercase hex; the fixed .provenance/state store path; a scope id ScopeId accepts; a full 40- or 64-character lowercase commit id, never an abbreviation; a sha256: digest; a correlation with both parts filled if present. A JSON Schema replica exists in the cli schema handler; a conformance test pushes 59 boundary values through both and asserts agreeing verdicts. One known divergence (schema_version 1.0) is tracked in beads.
rules.statement: GraphReference::validate refuses any reference whose fields deviate from the issued shape

rules.description: The badge must not let resolved lie: plain Resolved appears exactly when a decision or rule stands behind the requirement, and the admission appears exactly when none does. Non-resolved statuses never gain the suffix. Proven over every status with the count axes bucketed to zero, one, and many.
rules.statement: A resolved requirement with no decisions and no rules is labelled Resolved (no decisions or rules), never plain Resolved

rules.description: Blank means empty or whitespace; refused, never repaired. Enforced at deserialization via a wire-shape TryFrom, so the CLI create path and import share one gate. The reference is deliberately not resolved against the graph - it may cite legislation, a file, or a conversation the graph will never see; the rule decides something was named, not that it exists.
rules.statement: A resolution input's reference and summary must not be blank; a field that names nothing locates nothing

rules.name: Retired bindings excluded from active views
rules.statement: Active coverage, stale, plan, and wiki views exclude retired bindings. Export, import, check, and graph references preserve them

rules.name: Only a later run clears review
rules.statement: A verification run clears only reviews raised before it ran. Clearing writes the run and the time onto the record and keeps the reason

rules.name: One review record per affected rule
rules.statement: A requirement statement change writes one review record per produced rule, naming the field, its value before and after, and the change time

rules.name: A run retires only the key it reports
rules.statement: A verification run retires only a binding whose owner, file, and key it reports against a different rule. Absence from a run retires nothing, and no run retires another owner's binding

rules.name: Canonical Rust authored documents
rules.statement: The Rust authoring kernel orders sources and requirements by key and rules by serialized address with lexicographic UTF-8 byte order.

rules.name: Pure Rust authoring kernel
rules.description: The kernel can use pure core types and functions. It cannot read process or repository state.
rules.statement: Rust authoring build and materialize operations perform no file, environment, process, clock, repository, scanner, or store access.

rules.name: Scan bindings after relocation
rules.statement: The workspace-wide Rule binding scan runs after CLI SDK operations move to provenance-store.

rules.name: Trim Rust build-time text
rules.statement: Rust build-time content checks reject text that is empty after trimming, matching TypeScript requireText behavior.

rules.name: Audit before Rust crate publication
rules.statement: Rust crate publication starts only after the DR10 audit is complete and Ben records a separate go decision.

rules.name: Capture plan goldens before relocation
rules.statement: Rendered-plan goldens are captured before CLI SDK operations move to provenance-store.

rules.name: Recheck Cargo artifact dependencies
rules.statement: Rust SDK Plan work does not rely on Cargo artifact dependencies until primary-source evidence has been checked again.

rules.name: Recheck stable const string assertions
