rules.statement: Rust SDK Plan work does not rely on compile-time key assertions until stable Rust support for const string comparison and assertion is verified.

rules.name: Semantics-free Rust facade
rules.statement: The provenance-sdk facade delegates materialization, structural validation, address construction, identity, planning, and mutation to provenance-core or provenance-store.

rules.name: Store-owned persistent identity
rules.description: Id resolution includes local-to-shared migration, ownership checks, explicit-id validation, and resolution-dependent collision checks.
rules.statement: Only provenance-store determines persistent declaration identity.

rules.name: Store-owned Rust symbol resolution
rules.statement: Only provenance-store resolves an implementation symbol to a repository file for Rust SDK apply.

rules.name: Refuse unresolved Rust symbols
rules.statement: Rust SDK apply writes no state when an implementation symbol does not resolve to exactly one repository file.

rules.name: Round-trip Rust typed input
rules.statement: A Rust TypedSpec input round trip preserves every present field and the existing omission behavior.

rules.name: Record Rust verification failure first
rules.statement: When a Rust verification callback returns an error or unwinds, verification records the run as failed before it propagates the callback failure.

rules.name: Stable typed-spec wire acceptance
rules.statement: A protocol-4 typed-spec document receives the same accept-or-reject result after kernel extraction as it received before extraction.

rules.name: Stable first wire error
rules.statement: For a typed-spec document with more than one defect, kernel extraction preserves the first engine error class and text.

rules.name: Preserve decoded wire order
rules.statement: Wire ingestion returns resources and diagnostics in decoded document order and does not apply authored-document canonical ordering.

rules.description: A later version means a different layout that today's structs would half-read silently. One function guards the five core sites with byte-identical messages; the store's four sibling copies and the unguarded non-ideation read path are tracked in beads. Proven exhaustively over five kinds x versions 0, 1, 2, and u32 max.
rules.statement: Ideation records are read only at schema version one

rules.name: No install-time binary fetch
rules.statement: Installing a supported SDK selects a package-manager artifact for the host and does not download an executable from an install script

rules.name: Package supplies engine
rules.statement: When no explicit development override is configured, an SDK resolves and runs the engine supplied for its supported host by that language package

rules.name: Project discovery
rules.statement: When repository configuration is omitted, SDK operations use the nearest enclosing Provenance project or Git worktree root

rules.name: Protocol handshake before mutation
rules.statement: An SDK rejects an engine outside its supported protocol range before sending a state-changing command
Attaching one Rule declaration to several Requirements materializes one canonical Rule with a relationship to each Requirement

rules.description: A source pin locates; a reference commit identifies. The strict shape (exactly 40 or 64 lowercase) deliberately lives in rule_reference_wellformed - two rules sharing the word commit, split on purpose, not drift. Verified by property against a written-out character-set oracle.
rules.statement: A source commit pin is 7 to 64 hexadecimal characters, any case

rules.name: Sound contracted verb forms
rules.description: The finite matcher covers negative contractions and positive forms whose subject and suffix establish a contracted verb. It omits forms that need grammar or meaning choices, so a clean report does not establish complete Rule 4.2 coverage. An indeterminate quote model produces no strict finding.
rules.statement: An exact quote model reports each recognized contracted verb outside quoted text as a Rule 4.2 violation at its UTF-8 byte span
rules.source_section: Issue 9, Rule 4.2, pages 1-4-3 to 1-4-4 and Rule 8.6, page 1-8-7

rules.name: Descriptive sentence length
rules.statement: A descriptive sentence with a determinate count above 25 words produces one Rule 6.3 finding for its complete UTF-8 byte span

rules.name: Explicit quotation counting
rules.statement: A mechanically delimited quotation counts as one word in its containing sentence

rules.name: Hyphenated group counting
rules.statement: A hyphenated word or hyphenated group counts as one word

rules.name: Number counting
rules.statement: A mechanically identifiable number counts as one word when no Rule 8.6 meaning choice affects it

rules.name: Ordinary colon continuity
rules.statement: A colon in ordinary prose remains inside the descriptive sentence that contains it

rules.name: Paragraph sentence limit
rules.statement: When paragraph and sentence boundaries are clear, a paragraph with more than six sentences produces one Rule 6.6 finding for its full UTF-8 span

rules.name: Parenthetical counting
rules.statement: Parenthesized text counts once in its containing sentence and its contents count as a separate sentence

rules.name: Quoted text protection
rules.description: Balanced nonnested pairs produce exact protected spans. A malformed, nested, or mixed double-quote structure makes quote-dependent strict checks indeterminate.
rules.statement: Text inside a balanced pair of straight or curly double quotation marks produces no strict Rule 4.2 or Rule 8.1 finding

rules.name: Indeterminate semantic count
rules.statement: A sentence with a Rule 8.6 meaning choice produces no strict Rule 6.3 finding

rules.name: No semicolons in descriptive text
rules.description: An indeterminate quote model produces no strict finding.
rules.statement: An exact quote model reports each semicolon outside quoted text as a Rule 8.1 violation at its UTF-8 byte span
rules.source_section: Issue 9, Rule 8.1, page 1-8-1 and Rule 8.6, page 1-8-7

rules.statement: Statement analysis checks only new Requirement and Rule records and records whose statement bytes differ from the comparison base

rules.name: Agent STE dictionary acquisition
rules.description: Agent setup can use the direct official ASD asset. It does not require a person to complete the request form.
rules.statement: Agent onboarding downloads the official PDF when the project has no imported Issue 9 dictionary

rules.name: STE asset fallback
rules.description: The fallback uses the public route selected by STEMG. It does not search for a new hidden asset.
rules.statement: If the official PDF asset is unavailable, agent onboarding directs the user to the official request form
rules.source_section: Request a copy of ASD-STE100 Issue 9

rules.name: Credit the STE stewards
rules.description: The request page is the primary public acquisition link. The direct asset is an agent onboarding implementation detail.
rules.statement: Product text credits ASD as owner, identifies STEMG as maintainer, and links to the official request page
rules.source_document: STEMG ASD-STE100 copyright and legal notice

rules.name: Link likely STE defects
rules.description: This gives a user the steward's supported route for a proposed dictionary correction.
rules.statement: A likely dictionary defect report includes the official STEMG change-form link

rules.name: Limit STE product claims
rules.description: Provenance does not claim certification, affiliation, official status, or full ASD-STE100 conformance.
rules.statement: Product text names only the implemented Issue 9 checks and makes no compliance or endorsement claim

rules.name: Share concurrent STE downloads
rules.description: A lock prevents concurrent setup commands from requesting duplicate copies of the same asset.
rules.statement: Concurrent agent onboarding commands share one download of the same Issue 9 PDF

rules.name: Identify the STE downloader
rules.description: The steward can identify the client and its released version from a server request.
rules.statement: Each official PDF request identifies Provenance and its version in the HTTP User-Agent header

rules.name: Bound STE download retries
rules.description: A failed setup reports the failure after a configured retry bound. It does not repeatedly request the source.
rules.statement: The official PDF downloader stops after a fixed number of failed attempts

rules.name: Separate STE dictionary findings
rules.description: A word can be approved only for a specified meaning and part of speech. Technical terms are not in the general dictionary.
rules.statement: Dictionary checks report approved, unapproved, unknown, and uncertain uses as different result categories
rules.source_section: Dictionary meanings, parts of speech, and technical terms

rules.name: Record STE import identity
rules.description: These values identify both the input and the extraction result without putting either data set in project configuration.
rules.statement: Each imported dictionary records its Issue number, source digest, extracted-data digest, and extractor version

rules.name: Reuse imported STE dictionary
rules.description: The project records enough information to find and validate the imported dictionary. Normal checks use that local data.
rules.statement: A project reuses its imported dictionary for later checks and does not download the PDF during each CI run

rules.description: The index file holds extracted dictionary data outside distributed files. A load recomputes the digest over the stored entries and compares it with the identity record. A mismatch fails closed and the caller must import the PDF again. This makes rule_ste_dictionary_import_reuse safe against corrupt or edited index files.
rules.statement: A stored dictionary index loads only when its recomputed data digest equals the recorded extracted-data digest

rules.name: Interactive STE dictionary acquisition
rules.description: The user completes the official human download flow. Provenance imports the selected Issue 9 PDF after the download.
rules.statement: Interactive onboarding directs the user to the official request form and imports the PDF that the user selects
rules.source_section: Request a copy of ASD-STE100 Issue 9

rules.name: No operational STE download
rules.description: Only the onboarding acquisition path can use the network. All later operations require reusable local data.
rules.statement: Normal checks, builds, tests, and CI runs never download the official PDF

rules.name: Do not distribute STE dictionary data
rules.description: The product provides import code and configuration only. The official PDF and the derived local index stay outside distributed product files.
rules.statement: Provenance distributions do not contain the official PDF or dictionary data extracted from it

rules.name: Dictionary PDF validation
rules.statement: Dictionary extraction accepts only a decodable Issue 9 PDF that contains Part 2 dictionary pages

rules.description: The project state holds one dictionary reference with the issue number, source digest, data digest, and extractor version. The index file with the dictionary content stays in the machine data directory, or in the directory that PROVENANCE_STE100_INDEX_DIR names. A missing or failed index load produces no vocabulary findings and no network request, because normal checks never download. Interactive and agent onboarding in provenance-l3m.14 will repair a missing index.
rules.statement: Statement checks use the project dictionary reference only when its index loads from the machine data directory
rules.source_section: project reference and machine index separation

rules.name: Dictionary structure validation
rules.statement: Extracted dictionary data loads only when its approved and unapproved row counts match the expected Issue 9 totals and its entries keep nondecreasing first-letter order

rules.description: Matching folds case and compares each token and phrase against every imported word form, longest phrase first. Text inside balanced double quotation marks is protected, like the other strict checks. A token that touches a digit or an underscore is part of an identifier and produces no result. A word in both status sets is an uncertain use, and a word in neither set is an unknown use. Those categories report without a strict finding, because Rules 1.2 and 1.3 need a meaning choice and technical nouns and verbs are outside the dictionary.
rules.statement: A word with only unapproved forms in the imported dictionary produces a strict Rule 1.1 finding
Requirement and Rule creation leaves canonical graph state unchanged when a new statement has a deterministic ASD-STE100 violation

rules.description: Apply and dry-run analyze the same final staged Requirement and Rule state against the current canonical base and return the same structured diagnostics.
rules.statement: Scope import rejects staged Rule 8.1 findings before canonical state changes

rules.description: The report is informational and does not decide the open repository-wide failure policy.
rules.statement: Repository check reports Rule 8.1 findings only for Requirement and Rule statements that differ from Git HEAD

rules.description: The merge ancestor is the comparison base and the existing three-way record merge selects the candidate state.
rules.statement: The JSONL merge driver rejects changed Requirement and Rule statements with Rule 8.1 findings before it writes the result path
The sdk check-statement request returns the exact provenance-ste100 descriptive-text Report for its statement
The sdk check-statement request does not resolve or modify a repository
The sdk check-statement request accepts only one JSON object with a statement string and rejects unknown fields

rules.name: Analyze changed typed statements
rules.description: The analyzer runs after in-memory Requirement and Rule reconciliation. Unchanged declarations and updates to other fields do not recheck their statements.
rules.statement: SDK reconciliation analyzes Rule 8.1 only for Requirement and Rule declarations that are created or have a statement field change

rules.name: Reject typed apply atomically
rules.description: A rejected apply leaves all persisted graph bytes unchanged.
rules.statement: SDK apply rejects a detected Rule 8.1 violation before it writes canonical state, edges, or bindings

rules.name: Plan and apply diagnostic parity
rules.description: Each diagnostic identifies the declaration address, resource kind, statement field, ASD-STE100 Issue 9 Rule 8.1, disposition, exact UTF-8 byte span, and message.
rules.statement: SDK plan and rejected SDK apply expose the same ordered typed Rule 8.1 diagnostics for one reconciled specification

rules.description: The write-time enforcement of the exactly-one-active-thread invariant, by reconciliation rather than refusal: resolved and archived threads and other records are untouched, and the publication lock serializes concurrent posts so the race cannot happen. Verified by property through the real write path. Known gap tracked in beads: import writes threads wholesale with no thread validation. Supersedes imported rule PROV-IDEATE-032 jointly with rule_canonical_thread.
rules.statement: When a write picks a record's canonical thread, the same write archives every other active thread of that record
Building a fluent typed specification does not mutate its declarations or canonical Provenance state
A typed implementation link is accepted only when static analysis resolves its source expression to one repository file and exported symbol

rules.name: Exact development dependency
rules.statement: The initializer installs the matching Provenance SDK release as an exact development dependency with the selected package manager.

rules.name: Package-manager selection
rules.description: If lockfiles identify more than one package manager, the initializer requires an explicit option. The current supported managers are npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun, Deno, and Nub.
rules.statement: The initializer uses this package manager order: explicit option, packageManager field, unambiguous lockfile, invoking user agent, and npm fallback.

rules.name: Validated initialization
rules.statement: The initializer reports success only after the installed SDK engine creates the default scope and validates the new Provenance state.

rules.name: Verification binding identity key
rules.statement: A verification binding's identity is the verification owner, the canonical rule, and an owner-local key. A change to repository path, symbol, or method updates the same binding

rules.name: One list of verification method words
rules.statement: The verifies macro and the scanner accept exactly the same verification method words: exhaustion, property, examples, conformance, construction, and proof. proof claims a machine-checked proof outside the test runner, bridged to the implementation by the marked site.

rules.name: Verification runs are derived cache data
rules.description: Cache placement per docs/cache.md. That a run must cite an existing Rule is from docs/typescript-sdk-poc.md.
rules.statement: A verification run is derived cache data that cites an existing rule and never changes Git-tracked canonical state

rules.name: Search, domains, traceability order
rules.statement: At 1440x900 and 390x844, the homepage search control must precede every repeated domain row, and the traceability call to action must follow the domain section.
rules.source_section: Human disposition of Directions A-C; candidate constraints 1-3 and 8

rules.name: Plain homepage language
rules.description: Amended 2026-08-10: enforcement is scoped to generator-authored chrome. The checker must not reject a build because a user named a scope or domain 'corpus' or 'Atlas'; their words are their own.
rules.statement: Reader-facing generator-authored copy must use everyday labels for the project, documentation, records, and missing evidence; generator chrome must not use the word 'corpus'. User-authored content is quoted as written, whatever words it uses.

rules.name: Honest homepage search coverage
rules.statement: Until offline search indexes resolutions and sources, homepage search copy must state that it covers requirements and rules.

rules.name: Exact compact traceability summary
rules.description: Amended 2026-08-10: the findings route folded into the Unfinished page, so the count links there. One page owns unfinished work; no duplicate route says the same thing two ways.
rules.statement: The homepage must show one exact count of unfinished items linked to the Unfinished page, which carries every gap, orphan, and open question, and must render no individual gap cards.
rules.source_section: Candidate constraint 4; human graft from Direction C

rules.description: Replacing a directory destroys everything in it. A marker that exists but does not prove ownership (foreign generator, unsupported version, oversized, malformed, or not a regular file) is always a refusal, never a licence to overwrite, whichever policy asked. Proven exhaustively over all 28 policy x marker x emptiness cases.
rules.statement: The wiki replaces a directory only when its marker proves this generator published it, when the directory is empty, or when it is the generator-owned default output

rules.description: The known hosts are GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket; with no remote or a self-hosted one, code references stay plain text because a repo-relative link would 404 against the wiki's own routes. Verified by property over generated references crossed with remote states, and by exhaustion over the host x line-anchor table. Amended 2026-08-10: a bare dotted token with no directory and no line group is prose, never a file path - payroll.rs alone stays plain text; src/payroll.rs or payroll.rs:12 links. One predicate governs whole-field references and free-text spans alike.
rules.statement: A reference renders as a link only when the link would work: a web address as it stands, or a file path a known code host can turn into a real address; everything else stays plain text

rules.name: Agent maintains traceability
rules.statement: A development agent completing a workflowd change updates applicable obligations and verification relationships in the same change without a separate human graph-repair pass

rules.name: Plan explains workflowd impact
rules.statement: Planning a changed workflowd obligation identifies its affected Rules, implementation sites, verification sites, and evidence requiring review without changing canonical state

rules.name: Model obligations, not functions
rules.statement: The workflowd typed spec contains behavioural obligations chosen from product intent and not one declaration for every implementation function
